claim_formal: ∀ abelian variety A/Q̄ with good reduction A_0 at w, ∀ rational Hodge class γ ∈ H^{2r}, ∀ divisors D_1..D_{d-r} on A_0, ∃ q ∈ ℚ: Tr_ℓ(γ_{0,ℓ}·∏c_1(D_i)) = q (all ℓ≠p) ∧ Tr_p(γ_{0,p}·∏c_1^cris(D_i)) = q

quote_A.text: the pairing of a rational Hodge class with any complementary product of divisor classes on the reduction is the same rational number in every prime-to-p realization and in crystalline cohomology

quote_B.text: We prove Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties, including residue characteristic 2.

notes: Matrix: the ∃q is a rationality/realization-independence property, so M1; M2 is the alternative reading. Corollary: each specialized Hodge class is represented by one rational algebraic cycle in all realizations; the summary says this needs result 032 (another model output), but that is not the headline.

claim_formal: ∀ A,B ⊆ ℕ₀ with |A|,|B| ≥ 2: (A+B) △ 𝒫 is infinite

quote_A.text: no set differing from the primes by finitely many elements can be written as $`A+B`$, where A and B are sets of nonnegative integers with at least two elements each

quote_B.text: We prove Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture

notes: The Lean also states the two-infinite-summands reduction (twoInfiniteSummandsImpossible).

claim_formal: ∃ c₁,c₂>0, b₀: ∀ b ≥ b₀: c₁ log log b ≤ N(b) := max_{1≤a<b} min #{distinct unit fractions summing to a/b} ≤ c₂ log log b

quote_A.text: There are absolute constants $c_1,c_2>0$ and $b_0$ such that, for every integer $b\ge b_0$, \[ c_1\log\log b\le N(b)\le c_2\log\log b. \]

quote_B.text: is recorded as Erd\H{o}s Problem~304 \cite{Bloom304}. Vose subsequently obtained $N(b)\ll\sqrt{\log b}$

notes: The lower bound is classical (Erdős); the new content is the upper bound O(log log b). M8 if one counts only the new half. Threshold b₀ and constants are not explicit, so neither effective nor ineffective is marked. Corollaries: log log F(k) = Θ(k), and log log v(k) = Θ(k) (Erdős #293 direction).

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ singular klt germ (X,x) of dim n with zero boundary: n̂vol(x,X) ≤ 2(n−1)^n, with equality ⇔ (X,x)_an ≅ ODP {z₀²+…+z_n²=0}

quote_A.text: a singular n-dimensional germ has normalized volume at most $`2(n-1)^n`$, with equality precisely at an analytic ordinary double point

quote_B.text: We prove the ordinary-double-point gap conjecture for boundary-zero complex algebraic klt germs in every dimension

notes: The every-dimension induction uses the fourfold companion (also model output, in the family) as its base case. The conjecture is also K-stability problem list Problem 33; P1 was chosen because it is the named Spotti–Sun conjecture. Corollary: global volume bounds for K-semistable Fano varieties.

claim_formal: ∃ rank-2 algebraic bundle G on S=ℙ¹×ℙ¹: (∀ m ≥ 1: E_m = f_m^*G ⊗ O(1,1) is ample) ∧ ∃ m₀ ∀ m ≥ m₀: E_m admits no smooth Hermitian metric with strictly Griffiths-positive curvature

quote_A.text: There is an algebraic vector bundle $G$ of rank two on $S$ such that, for every positive integer $m$, the bundle \[ E_m=f_m^*G\otimes P \] is ample.

quote_B.text: We give counterexamples to Griffiths' conjecture in rank two on the quadric surface

notes: m₀ is obtained by compactness and is explicitly ineffective. The Lean SourceMainTheorem is truncated in the input but starts ∃ G ∃ E with the power-pullback structure, consistent with the headline.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth Fano manifold X of dim n>0, Picard number ρ, pseudoindex ι: ρ(ι−1) ≤ n, with equality ⇔ X ≅ (ℙ^{ι−1})^ρ

quote_A.text: every positive-dimensional smooth complex Fano manifold of dimension n, Picard number ρ, and pseudoindex ι satisfies $`\rho(\iota-1)\le n`$. Equality holds precisely for the product of ρ copies of $`\mathbb P^{\iota-1}`$.

quote_B.text: We prove the generalized Mukai conjecture

notes: A sharp bound with the equality case classified, so M9; M6 is the alternative for the equality part.

claim_formal: ∀ ε∈(0,1) ∃ N₀ ∀ N ≥ N₀ ∃ signs ε_k ∈ {±1}: (1−ε)√N ≤ |Σ_{k<N} ε_k z^k| ≤ (1+ε)√N for all |z|=1

quote_A.text: For every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ there is an integer $N_0$ such that, for every integer $N\ge N_0$, there are signs $\varepsilon_0,\ldots,\varepsilon_{N-1}$ for which

quote_B.text: Their binary merit factors tend to infinity, disproving Turyn's bounded-merit-factor conjecture.

notes: The headline is an existence (M2) whose witnesses refute the real-sign Erdős fixed-gap conjecture (inf m_N ≥ 1+c) and Turyn's conjecture, so M3 by precedence. The problem source could also be read as P3 (Erdős 1957 Problems 22/26) or P2. The ultraflat paper builds on the two earlier model papers (minimal maxima; v2 lower envelope). The Lean covers only the upper half (m_N → 1) and finite-L^p flatness, not the two-sided ultraflat statement, hence weaker.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 4, ∀ convex body K ⊂ ℝⁿ: |ΠK|/|K|^{n−1} ≥ κ_{n−1}^n κ_n^{2−n}, with equality ⇔ K is an ellipsoid

quote_A.text: For every integer $n\ge4$ and every convex body $K\subset\R^n$, \begin{equation}\label{eq:main} \frac{|\Pi K|}{|K|^{n-1}} \ge \kappa_{n-1}^{\,n}\kappa_n^{\,2-n}. \end{equation} Equality holds if and only if $K=a+TB_2^n$

quote_B.text: This proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in these dimensions.

notes: The conjecture is posed for n ≥ 3; this proves n ≥ 4 (rule 6 → O5). Together with Chen et al.'s n=3 theorem it gives the full conjecture. Secondary result: a product-of-simplices counterexample to Brannen's simplex maximum in dimension 20, with exponential excess, though Feng et al. had already refuted it for d ≥ 9.

claim_formal: ∃ finite family of cylinders B_i+ℝu_i with compact triangular bases covering the regular tetrahedron K (A_min(K)=√2) with Σ|B_i| < A_min(K)/2 (and Σ|B_i|/|π_{u_i^⊥}K| < 1/2)

quote_A.text: A regular tetrahedron admits a finite cylinder covering with compact triangular perpendicular bases whose total area is less than half its minimum orthogonal projection area.

quote_B.text: This disproves the half-area cylinder-covering conjecture.

notes: Two posed statements are refuted: Bang's half-area question (Bezdek Problem 3.1, also Verreault Question 4.14) and Bezdek–Khan's 1-Codimensional Cylinder Covering Conjecture. P1 was chosen for the named conjecture; P2 fits the Bang question. Several manuscripts give alternative constructions plus general finite-approximation tools. The Lean TriangularCovering states A_min=√2, the ε-asymptotic covers and the normalized counterexample.

claim_formal: ∃ L ∈ P (deterministic poly-time TM) ∀ A>0 ∃ N_A ∀ n ≥ N_A: every OR–AND–OR circuit computing L∩{0,1}ⁿ has > 2^{A√n} gates

quote_A.text: We construct a language in deterministic polynomial time whose n-bit membership function requires $`2^{\omega(\sqrt n)}`$ gates in an unbounded-fan-in OR–AND–OR circuit.

quote_B.text: This is the depth-three lower-bound problem discussed by Gurumukhani, Paturi, Pudl\'ak, Saks, and Talebanfard~\cite[Section~1.1]{GPPST24} and still identified as open

notes: Matrix: a one-sided circuit-size lower bound with a rate (M8); M10 (complexity status) is plausible. Problem/outcome: settles the open ω(√n) question (P2/O1). It could also be read as P4/O7 (record exponent improved), since the stronger 2^{n^{1/2+ε}} question of HJP95 stays open.

claim_formal: inf{α : ∃ deterministic poly-time α-approximation for finite rational metric k-median} = 1+2/e (assuming P≠NP); unconditionally ∀ ε>0 ∃ poly-time (1+2/e+ε)-approximation

quote_A.text: Under $`P\ne NP`$, the infimum approximation factor in this model is therefore $`1+2/e`$.

quote_B.text: For every fixed ε > 0, we give a deterministic polynomial-time $`(1+2/e+\varepsilon)`$-approximation for finite rational metric k-median

notes: The P≠NP condition applies to the threshold; the matching hardness (1+2/e) is classical and conditional, and the algorithm is unconditional. Rule 7 (exact determination of a record number) gives M9/O1; O6 is the alternative because of the P≠NP condition. The prefix could be ∀∃ (∀ε ∃ algorithm) with M10 if the algorithm is taken as the headline. The second manuscript gives a randomized (2−σ) recovery result. The Lean covers both the threshold (under PNeNP) and the algorithm.

claim_formal: ∀ fixed one-writable-tape TM M (with read-only heads, accessor) ∃ simulator N ∃ c,e ∀ x, T ≥ 2 (access condition): N computes M's control/halting outcome at time T in ≤ c·T^{2/5}·log^e(T+2) space

quote_A.text: a fixed deterministic Turing machine with one writable tape and head can be simulated in $`O(T^{2/5}\mathop{\mathrm{polylog}}\nolimits (T+2))`$ work-space bits

quote_B.text: This improves the square-root space exponent for one-tape machines, answering Williams's question for this model.

notes: Matrix: a space upper bound with a rate (M8); M10 (class inclusion / algorithm existence) is equally plausible. Williams asked whether the one-tape √T exponent can be lowered by a constant, so this is P2/O1; P4/O7 is an alternative reading (exponent 1/2 → 2/5, not the optimum). The model carries an accessor condition.

claim_formal: ∀ finite weakly reversible network, ∀ positive rates, ∀ positive stoichiometric class P ∃ compact convex forward-invariant K_P ⊂ P ∀ x⁰ ∈ P ∃ T(x⁰): x(t) ∈ K_P for t ≥ T(x⁰)

quote_A.text: For every positive stoichiometric class $P$ there is a nonempty compact convex set $K_P\subset P$ with the following properties.

quote_B.text: We prove the permanence conjecture for finite weakly reversible mass-action systems with fixed positive reaction rates.

notes: Matrix: the conclusion is existence of a common absorbing set (M2); M1 is the alternative if permanence is read as a property. The family also proves the boundedness and persistence conjectures (companion paper, with trajectory-dependent bounds). The Lean global_bounded_persistent_solution states only that trajectory-dependent version, which is weaker than classwise permanence.

claim_formal: ∃ explicit bipartite H (35 vertices, 66 edges; incidence graph of 22 triples on 13 points) ∃ finite simple graph G with an edge: t(H,G) < p(G)^66

quote_A.text: There is a finite simple undirected graph \(G\) with at least one edge such that \[ t(H,G)<p(G)^{66}. \]

quote_B.text: We disprove Sidorenko's conjecture with a bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges

notes: The same H also disproves the Skokan–Thoma forcing conjecture (corollary), with an amplification corollary.

claim_formal: ∃ C>0 ∀ k ≥ 1 ∀ finite loopless k-edge-connected multigraph G (|V| ≥ 2) ∃ spanning tree T: ∀ ∅≠S⊊V: |δ_T(S)| ≤ (C/k)|δ_G(S)|

quote_A.text: every finite \(k\)-edge-connected undirected multigraph without loops and with at least two vertices has a spanning tree \(T\) satisfying

quote_B.text: This resolves the strong thin tree conjecture.

notes: The outer ∃C is a uniform constant and is not counted as a main object. The companion paper gives a deterministic polynomial-time construction, which the second Lean also covers. Matrix: existence of a tree (M2); M8 if the C/k rate is taken as the content.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ nontrivial increasing vertex-permutation-invariant graph property 𝒫, ∀ ε∈(0,1/2): p_{1−ε}(𝒫) − p_ε(𝒫) ≤ 2^19 log(1/(2ε))/(log n)²  [and for r-uniform hypergraphs, width O_r((log n)^{−r/(r−1)})]

quote_A.text: p_{1-\varepsilon}(\mathcal P)-p_\varepsilon(\mathcal P) \le \frac{2^{19}}{(\log n)^2}\log\frac1{2\varepsilon}.

quote_B.text: For increasing properties, it gives the corresponding threshold-width bound with exponent $`r/(r-1)`$, proving the hypergraph threshold-width conjecture of Friedgut and Kalai.

notes: The headline covers both the Friedgut–Kalai graph conjecture (explicit constant 2^19, effective) and the hypergraph version (C_r not explicit). The hypergraph paper reuses the companion graph paper's method. The order (log n)^{-2} is known to be optimal for graphs (clique example), so M9 is an alternative. The Lean covers only the graph case, hence weaker. The variance–influence bound holds without monotonicity.

claim_formal: ∃ finite-dimensional unital ℂ-algebra A ∀ m ≥ 1 ∃ f.d. left A-module N_m: 2m−2 ≤ pd_A N_m < ∞; hence findim A = ∞

quote_A.text: There is a finite-dimensional unital complex algebra \(A\) such that, for every integer \(m\ge1\), there is a finite-dimensional left \(A\)-module \(N_m\) with

quote_B.text: This disproves the little finitistic-dimension conjecture.

notes: Corollary: extreme left–right asymmetry, and failure of injective generation (also in the Lean).

claim_formal: ∀ b ≥ 6, ∀ finite-dimensional complex V: ∃ GL(V)-equivariant injection Sym⁶(Sym^b V) ↪ Sym^b(Sym⁶ V)  (⇔ h_b[h_6] − h_6[h_b] Schur-positive)

quote_A.text: For every integer \(b\ge6\) and every finite-dimensional complex vector space \(V\), there is a \(\GL(V)\)-equivariant injection

quote_B.text: We prove the sixth-symmetric-power case of Foulkes' conjecture.

notes: This settles the a=6 case of Foulkes' conjecture, which is posed for all a ≤ b (O5). The existence of an injection is equivalent to Schur-positivity, so M1 with prefix ∀ is an alternative. The proof uses the companion quadratic-stabilization paper (b ≥ 30) and Evseev–Paget–Wildon computations (b ≤ 13). The Lean covers only the companion theorem, surjectivity of the canonical Foulkes–Howe map for b ≥ a(a−1), hence different. That theorem also answers Landsberg Problem 7.19.

claim_formal: ∀ α>0, ∀ bounded Borel f: lim_N E p_N(f) = inf_q{αV_f(q)+S_I(q)} and p_N(f) → that value in probability (Gaussian Ising perceptron); likewise for the spherical perceptron with bounded continuous φ

quote_A.text: \lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb E p_N(f) =\mathcal P_f(\alpha) :=\inf_{q\in\mathcal Q}\{\alpha V_f(q)+S_{\mathrm I}(q)\}.

quote_B.text: We determine the limiting free energy of the Ising perceptron with independent Gaussian patterns for every bounded Borel log-potential, at every fixed positive temperature and pattern density.

notes: Problem: an open determination with physics (Gardner) predictions, where earlier rigorous work covered only small density (P2). O8 (extending small-density theorems) is an alternative. The family also covers the bi-orthogonally invariant spherical model and a jamming theorem at margin −1: sharp SAT threshold and gap/force exponent laws. The Lean covers the spherical free energy fully but only finiteness of the Ising variational value, hence weaker.

claim_formal: ∀ deterministic spectra Λ_N with μ_N ⇒ μ compact and extreme eigenvalues → support edges, U_N Haar on O(N): lim E P_N = lim P_N (a.s.) = inf_p{S(p)+G_1(p)}

quote_A.text: \lim_{N\to\infty}\E P_N =\lim_{N\to\infty}P_N =\mathcal F(\mu) :=\inf_{p\in\cP}\{S(p)+G_1(p)\}

quote_B.text: We solve this problem for every fixed temperature when the limiting spectral law is compactly supported and there are no asymptotic outliers.

notes: Earlier rigorous formulas needed high temperature. The problem is an open determination, not a named conjecture (P2); O8 is an alternative. Corollaries: the external-field version and the zero-field ground-state energy. The Lean is truncated in the input; it appears to formalize the pressure formula including external fields, so 'same' is tentative.

claim_formal: ∀ hyperbolic group G with ∂G ≅ S²: ∃ homomorphism ρ: G → Isom(ℍ³) with proper cocompact action and finite kernel

quote_A.text: every hyperbolic group whose boundary is homeomorphic to the two-sphere admits a proper cocompact isometric action on hyperbolic three-space with finite kernel

quote_B.text: This resolves Cannon's conjecture positively.

notes: Corollary: a torsion-free G is π₁ of a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold.

claim_formal: ∀ finite X, ∀ r ∈ F(X): (⟨X|r⟩ contains no BS(m,n), m,n ≠ 0) → ⟨X|r⟩ is word-hyperbolic

quote_A.text: If the one-relator group $G=\langle X\mid r\rangle$ contains no subgroup isomorphic to $\operatorname{BS}(m,n)$ for any nonzero integers $m,n$, then $G$ is word-hyperbolic.

quote_B.text: We prove Gersten's conjecture

notes: The converse is classical, so the result is effectively a characterization (M5 alternative). Gersten posed it as a question in a problem paper; it is conventionally called a conjecture. Second headline (companion): every hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually compact special. With Kielak–Linton this gives Wise's virtual free-by-cyclic conjecture for these groups.

claim_formal: ∀ N ≥ 2: dim Ker H_N = 1 for the relative SU(N) BFSS Hamiltonian (∃! normalizable zero-energy state)

quote_A.text: For every integer \(N\ge2\), \[ \dim\Ker H_N=1. \]

quote_B.text: This establishes the threshold-bound-state conjecture.

notes: Unique existence of a bound state is read as ∃! with M2; M9 (the exact value dim Ker = 1) is the alternative. Companion result: for SU(2) there are infinitely many positive eigenvalues with L² eigenvectors, refuting the original BFSS paper's exclusion (an O2-type secondary result).

claim_formal: ∀ 4d unitary positive-energy QFT satisfying the operational hypotheses (bounded local net, field reconstruction, discrete bounded-below scaling spectrum with finite multiplicities, finite scaling support, physical local dilatation current): ∃ physical dim-2 scalar L with ∂·V^{(3)} = □L, so T has a symmetric conserved traceless improvement with the same charges (local conformal Ward identities)

quote_A.text: Under these hypotheses, the stress tensor admits a symmetric, conserved, traceless improvement with unchanged translation and Lorentz charges.

quote_B.text: We prove that scale symmetry implies local conformal symmetry for a class of four-dimensional unitary, positive-energy quantum field theories

notes: The headline is 'scale ⇒ conformal' (M1 implication); the theorem's form is existence of an improvement scalar (M2). The scale-vs-conformal question is a long-standing conjecture or open problem, settled here only for a class under strong framework hypotheses and only locally (no global conformal action), hence O5. P2 is an alternative for the problem type. The hypotheses are framework assumptions, not unproved conjectures, so conditional_on was not used.

claim_formal: ∃ separable unital complex C*-algebra A with a normalized 2-quasitrace ∃ positive contractions a,b ∀ normalized 2-quasitrace τ: τ(a+b) − τ(a) − τ(b) ≥ 1/144

quote_A.text: There exist a separable unital complex \(C^*\)-algebra \(A\), admitting a normalized \(2\)-quasitrace, and positive contractions \(a,b\in A\) such that every normalized \(2\)-quasitrace \(\tau\) on \(A\) satisfies

quote_B.text: We refute Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture

notes: Corollary (Milhøj–Rørdam question): the minimal tensor product of two unital simple stably finite C*-algebras can be properly infinite, with one factor C_r^*(F_2).

claim_formal: ∀ nontrivial smooth knot K ⊂ S³, ∀ r,s ∈ ℚ∪{∞}: S³_r(K) ≅⁺ S³_s(K) → r = s

quote_A.text: Distinct Dehn surgery slopes on a nontrivial smooth knot never give orientation-preservingly homeomorphic manifolds.

quote_B.text: We prove the purely cosmetic surgery conjecture for knots in the three-sphere.

notes: Read as non-existence of purely cosmetic pairs (M4); M1 (implication r=s) is the alternative. The proof settles the remaining case (genus 2, slopes ±2) left by the Hanselman and Daemi–Lidman–Miller Eismeier reductions. The conjecture is also Kirby list Problem 1.81(A), so P3 is possible.

claim_formal: ∀ prime p ≥ 5: strong chromatic splitting fails at height 3 (the canonical map L_0L_{K(3)}S → L_0L_{K(2)}L_{K(3)}S is nonzero on π_{−3}); weak splitting fails at heights p (p ≥ 5) and p+1 (p ≥ 7); yet ∀ n ≥ 1, p > n+1: L_{n−1}L_{K(n)}S_p^∧ has a 2ⁿ-stage filtration with the predicted cofibers

quote_A.text: For every prime \(p\geq5\), the canonical map \begin{equation}\label{eq:main-map} \tau_{L_{K(3)}S}:L_0L_{K(3)}S\longrightarrow L_0L_{K(2)}L_{K(3)}S \end{equation} is nonzero on \(\pi_{-3}\).

quote_B.text: Nevertheless, for n ≥ 1 and $`p\gt n+1`$, the overlap $`L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge`$ admits a $`2^n`$-stage filtration by the predicted localized-sphere pieces.

notes: Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture (strong form, Barthel–Beaudry revision) is refuted at specific heights and primes, and a filtered replacement is proved, hence O3. M4 (no homotopy retraction) is an alternative matrix for the weak-splitting part. The family also shows failure of finite assembly at p=n=3.

claim_formal: ∃ countable uniformly discrete (d ≥ 1), unbounded, nonproper pointed metric space M: F(M) has AP ∧ ∀ λ ≥ 1: F(M) fails λ-BAP

quote_A.text: We construct a countable uniformly discrete metric space whose real Lipschitz-free space has the approximation property but fails the bounded approximation property, answering Kalton's question negatively.

quote_B.text: answering Kalton's question negatively

notes: Kalton's question is repeated in Godefroy–Ozawa and in Godefroy's survey (Problem 6.2); by rule 8 it stays P2. Corollaries: quantitative ℓ₁ renormings (in the Lean), and F(M) is not approximable (Kalton's nonlinear question).

claim_formal: ∀ closed connected 4-manifold X, ∀ smooth a.c.s. J: (∃ symplectic ω taming J) → ∃ symplectic ω' compatible with J

quote_A.text: every smooth almost complex structure on a closed four-manifold which is tamed by a symplectic form is compatible with a symplectic form

quote_B.text: This gives a positive solution to Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture.

notes: Corollary: a description of the compatible cone in terms of the taming cone; for b₂⁺=1 the taming and compatible cones coincide.

claim_formal: ∀ V ∈ (0,1): min{Per(E): E ⊂ ℝ³/ℤ³, |E|=V} = min{(36π)^{1/3}v^{2/3}, 2√(πv), 2} (v=min(V,1−V)), and the minimizers are exactly balls / geodesic tubes / slabs (or complements), with switches at 4π/81 and 1/π

quote_A.text: the minimum perimeter is \begin{equation} I_{\rm unit}(V)= \min\left\{(36\pi)^{1/3}v^{2/3},\ 2\sqrt{\pi v},\ 2\right\}.

quote_B.text: We prove the isoperimetric conjecture for the cubic flat three-torus and classify all minimizers

notes: Exact profile (M9) together with a classification of minimizers (M6 alternative). It is a specific torus, but V is a free parameter, so specific_instance was not used. The proof uses Milman's reduction to the two transition volumes and HPRR's tools.

claim_formal: ∀ reduced absolute Mumford–Shah minimizer (u,K) in a bounded Lipschitz Ω ⊂ ℝ² with g ∈ L^∞, ∀ x ∈ K: near x, K is a C^{1,α} arc through x, a C^{1,α} arc ending at x, or three C^{1,α} arcs meeting at 120°; and ∀ U ⋐ Ω only finitely many components of K meet U

quote_A.text: Every $x\in K$ has an interior neighborhood in which $K$ has one of the following forms, with $C^{1,\alpha}$ arcs for some $\alpha>0$:

quote_B.text: We prove the interior regularity assertion of the planar Mumford–Shah conjecture for reduced absolute minimizers with bounded fidelity data.

notes: Matrix: a local classification of the discontinuity set (M6); M1 (regularity property) is the alternative. Outcome: only the interior assertion is proved, with no finiteness up to ∂Ω, so O5 is an alternative to O1. Corollary: ∇u ∈ weak-L⁴_loc.
